candidate.answerReason: The cost is 80% of the list price and also 80% of the selling price, so the selling price equals the list price. Recovering the marked price from its 80% selling price gives 125% of list, agreeing with C.

methods.label: Track the percentage bases
methods.explanation:
Only percentages are involved, so take the list price to be \(100\) price units. Scaling all prices together leaves every stated percentage unchanged.

The merchant's cost is \(80\%\) of the list price, or \(80\) units. His profit must be \(20\%\) of the selling price, so the remaining \(80\%\) of the selling price covers his cost. Thus the selling price must be
\[
80\div0.80=100.
\]
After the customer receives a \(20\%\) discount, this selling price is \(80\%\) of the marked price. Therefore the marked price must be
\[
100\div0.80=125.
\]
Relative to the list price, that is
\[
\frac{125}{100}\cdot100\%=125\%.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
